items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: But when Petrillo was alive, the head of, in Chicago, and all that kind of stuff

ctx.x: What did the union have to say about that?

I’m going to not have a comment. The union, by that point was, how can I put it delicately? Lost their guts. They had made so many sweetheart deals with various things, that they really made a terrible mistake. But when Petrillo was alive, the head of, in Chicago, and all that kind of stuff, those days didn’t last that long but they were wonderful days as far as the musicians were concerned, because they said this is the way it’s going to be. It was “Achtung.” But then eventually it really was economics. ©…
Was the technology that was happening, did it have an effect also?
